reports.summary: Build A meets every spec requirement. It has four pages sharing a nav, a catalogue of 15 books with a genre filter whose state lives in the URL, events, and a Visit page with hours, address and an accessible contact form. It uses only plain HTML, CSS and JS with no external requests, and it is responsive at 360px. I ran the Playwright suite in a copy of the build and all 33 tests passed. My own probes confirmed that the filter works over file://, keyboard order and focus outlines are correct, and colour contrast passes AA. The defects are minor: events are hard-coded and will all have expired by 20 Dec 2026, the 'staff note' claim doesn't match the anonymous blurbs, staff picks are chosen mechanically, the empty state can't be reached, the tests depend on a global Playwright and a fixed Chrome path, and the visual design is somewhat plain. Overall it is a solid, well-tested, accessible small site.

defects.evidence: css/styles.css .header-inner has no max-width (the .container rule sets max-width: 64rem). Visible in H-shots/index.html-desktop.png: the brand is at x=24 while the h1 is at x=144.

defects.what: The home-page staff-pick links go to a genre filter, not to the named book. Clicking 'The Ninth Stair' opens a list of two mysteries with nothing that points to the book that was clicked.
defects.evidence: index.html:39-41 hrefs are books.html?genre=Mystery and similar. Books have no ids or anchors.

defects.what: The home page promises 'directions', but the Visit page gives only a vague lede and a decorative abstract SVG map with no landmarks or transit details.
defects.evidence: index.html:48 'Opening hours, directions and how to get in touch'. visit.html:59-65 is an aria-hidden SVG with three lines and the label 'Quill Street'.

defects.what: The visual design is plain: no book covers or imagery, and the home page is a single text column that leaves the right half of the desktop viewport empty. Content depth is modest (12 books, 4 events, no event detail such as price or location).
defects.evidence: H-shots/index.html-desktop.png. index.html has only text sections.

defects.what: The tests depend on Playwright being installed globally and on Chrome being at the hardcoded path /usr/bin/google-chrome. There is no package.json, so the suite won't run on most machines without manual setup.
defects.evidence: tests/run.mjs:11 CHROME = '/usr/bin/google-chrome'. loadChromium falls back to npm root -g.

strengths: Meets every spec requirement: four pages share an identical nav with aria-current; a 12-title catalog across 6 genres; a working genre filter; hours, address and a contact form; no external requests; no horizontal overflow at 360px, even at 200% font size.

The filter is done well: aria-pressed toggle buttons, a polite live-region count, state kept in ?genre= with pushState/popstate for back and forward, and safe fallback for unknown or differently cased values.

The form follows accessibility best practice: real labels, novalidate with custom inline errors, aria-invalid and aria-describedby that combine the hint and the error, focus moves to the first invalid field, whitespace-only input and over-long input are rejected, and the success message honestly says nothing was sent.

Accessibility basics are solid: skip link, focusable main, a visible focus ring with a separate colour on the dark header, prefers-reduced-motion support, a decorative SVG hidden from assistive technology, logical heading levels, and colour pairs that meet WCAG AA.
The mobile menu is keyboard-friendly, closes on Escape and returns focus to the toggle, and resets when the viewport crosses the desktop breakpoint.
31 meaningful headless-Chrome tests cover behaviour (filter URL state, hostile inputs, form validation, overflow, contrast, console and off-origin checks). All passed locally.
The JavaScript is small and readable, and the content (titles, blurbs, events with correct weekdays) is consistent across pages.
reports.summary: Build H is a clean, spec-compliant static site with strong accessibility and an unusually thorough test suite. I ran `node tests/run.mjs` in the copy at /tmp/inspect-website-bookshop-H and got 31 passed, 0 failed. No blocker or major defects were found. The genre filter is robust, with URL state, back/forward support and fallback for bad values. The contact form handles errors well and is accessible. The main weaknesses are product polish: the design is plain and has no imagery, the desktop header doesn't line up with the content, the staff-pick links only filter by genre, the 'directions' promise isn't backed by content, and the content is fairly thin. The tests also depend on a globally installed Playwright and a hardcoded Chrome path.

strengths: Every spec item checked out: 4 pages with shared nav and aria-current, 15 books in 6 genres, events, and a visit page with hours table, address and contact form. A 360px probe showed scrollWidth 360 on all pages and zero external requests.

The genre filter is solid. The URL syncs both ways with replaceState, case and name aliases are normalised (?genre=Science%20Fiction becomes ?genre=science-fiction), the result count is announced via aria-live, and an empty-state message exists.

The contact form is accessible. It has visible labels, aria-describedby error text and aria-invalid, focuses the first invalid field, clears errors live, catches whitespace-only input, and says honestly that the form is a demo.

Accessibility basics are in place: skip link to a focusable main, 3px :focus-visible outline, 44px touch targets, prefers-reduced-motion support, a logical heading outline, and a table with row and column th scope. Text contrast is 7:1 or higher, the focus ring is 5.69:1 and input borders are 3.79:1.
Content is realistic and mostly consistent. Event dates fall on the stated weekdays, and the staff picks, catalogue and author talk cross-reference each other.
28 Playwright tests all pass. They cover filtering, URL handling, form validation, layout at 360px, no-network and page structure.
The code is small and clear: vanilla IIFEs, data separated from rendering, and rendering via textContent so there is no injection risk.
reports.summary: Build I meets every spec requirement with clean, idiomatic vanilla code. Its genre filter keeps the URL in sync, its contact form validation is accessible, and contrast and focus styles are strong. All 28 Playwright tests pass (`NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node --test tests/*.test.js`). My own 360px probe found no horizontal scroll and no external requests, and confirmed the skip link, filter and form error focus work. Every defect I found is minor: 'Wednesday' breaks mid-word in the mobile hours table, the README names a FEATURE_FLOW.md that doesn't exist, the evening-events wording contradicts the Thursday hours, the fallback email isn't a link, and the tests need a hardcoded global Chrome and Playwright setup. The visual design is tidy but plain, with no imagery. Overall this is a good, near-production small site.
